advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'a re-trigger restarts the retry budget' claim (adapter.py exhausted note + docs/review-policy.md) with the fact that `/rerun` does not call `reset_attempts` in this change (reset lands in bb9b).
evidence: adapter.py:259-260 exhausted note: "A contributor re-trigger or a new patchset restarts the retry budget."
docs/review-policy.md:76-79: "A stuck coverage-gap `-1` (an exhausted budget ...) is cleared by a maintainer re-trigger (`/rerun`; see `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`) or a new patchset"
voter.py:621-622 — `reset_attempts` is called ONLY on the write-on-success path after a vote lands; there is no reset on the force/`/rerun` path
app.py:236-283 `/rerun` handler sets `event["_rebar_force"]=True` and enqueues but never touches the attempt ledger
Ticket 0347 description: 'bb9b ... (lands second) ... implemented as "reset the shared review_attempts budget + force re-review"' — the reset is a future ticket, not this change
infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md has no mention of the retry budget (search for 'budget' returns no matches), yet review-policy.md points there for clearing it
advisory.finding: The retries-exhausted note (and docs/review-policy.md) tell operators that a `/rerun` re-trigger restarts/clears the retry budget, but this change never resets `review_attempts` on the force path — `reset_attempts` is only called after a *successful* vote (voter.py:622). A `/rerun` of a change stuck at an exhausted budget, while the infra fault persists, re-increments and re-escalates straight to the fail-closed -1 with no fresh deferrals; the actual re-trigger reset is deferred to the not-yet-landed bb9b ticket.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either (a) reword the note and docs to say only a NEW PATCHSET starts a fresh budget (a re-trigger's reset arrives with bb9b), or (b) call `store.reset_attempts` on the force path so the documented behavior holds now.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `gate-disabled` being RETRYABLE (bounded) is a deliberate revision of the ticket's 'gate-disabled is terminal' decision, and record the rationale; otherwise move it to the terminal set.
evidence: adapter.py:62: `RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS = frozenset({"review-error", "llm-unavailable", "scanner", "gate-disabled"})`
docs/review-policy.md:62-63 lists `gate-disabled` among the retryable sub-reasons that cast 'no vote at all'

Ticket 0347 comment (settled decisions): 'Terminal -> VOTE -1: ... gate-disabled — a configuration state that yields the IDENTICAL result forever, so a no-vote would make backfill retry it forever ... It votes -1'
Ticket 0347 later comment reaffirms 'gate-disabled is refused' for bb9b re-trigger, treating it as terminal
advisory.finding: `gate-disabled` is classified as RETRYABLE in both the implementation and docs, contradicting the operator-approved settled design on ticket 0347 that marks `gate-disabled` TERMINAL (vote -1 immediately) because a disabled gate 'yields the IDENTICAL result forever' and a no-vote would make backfill retry it forever. The bounded budget mitigates the infinite-loop concern, but the divergence from the recorded decision appears unacknowledged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` against non-positive values (clamp to the default) to match the shutdown_* getters, or document that 0 disables deferral.
evidence: config.py:243-245: `retryable_gap_max_attempts=_int_env("RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS", DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS)`
config.py:149-156 `_int_env` performs no range validation (returns any parseable int)
config.py:102/117 sibling getters guard `return val if val > 0 else float(DEFAULT_...)`
voter.py:549 `if attempts < cfg.retryable_gap_max_attempts:` — with a cap ≤0 the deferral branch is never taken
advisory.finding: `retryable_gap_max_attempts` is parsed via `_int_env` with no positivity guard, unlike the sibling `shutdown_drain_seconds`/`shutdown_cancel_seconds` getters which clamp non-positive values to the default. A `RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=0` (or negative) makes the first retryable gap escalate straight to the fail-closed -1 (`attempts=1 < 0` is False), silently disabling the deferral/recovery mechanism.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a voter test that drives a merge-path coverage-gap (`_merge_coverage_gap_decision`, no gap_reason) through `review_and_vote` and asserts it casts the fail-closed -1 immediately (status=='voted', not 'deferred').
evidence: voter.py:536-537 — `gap_reason = decision.get("gap_reason")` then `if gap_reason in adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS:` — the defer branch keys strictly on gap_reason
voter.py:219-228 — `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` returns a dict with `coverage_gap: True` but NO `gap_reason` key (relies on `.get` returning None to keep the immediate vote)
search for `merge-review` in tests/unit/test_review_bot.py returned no matches — no test drives the merge coverage-gap path through review_and_vote to assert `status == 'voted'` (not 'deferred')
PR message: 'the merge-path decision carries no gap_reason and keeps its immediate vote' — an asserted contract with no test
advisory.finding: No regression test pins the merge-path coverage-gap to its immediate fail-closed vote. The 0347 defer-vs-vote split keys on `decision.get("gap_reason") in adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS`; `_merge_coverage_gap_decision` (voter.py:214) deliberately omits `gap_reason` so a merge-review infra failure still votes -1 immediately. Nothing asserts this: if `gap_reason` were later added to the merge-path decision (or a merge sub-reason entered the retryable set), the merge change would defer vote-less forever and the reconciler would loop it — a silent regression of a behavior this diff explicitly introduces.
scenarios: A future edit adds a gap_reason to _merge_coverage_gap_decision; merge changes silently start deferring vote-less and never get a -1
A merge-path sub-reason is renamed to overlap RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_voter_merge_coverage_gap_votes_immediately`: produce a decision via the merge path (or a decision dict with `coverage_gap=True` and no `gap_reason`), run review_and_vote, and assert `res['status']=='voted'`, `vote_value==-1`, and `store.attempt_count(...)==0`.

When `store.record_attempt` raises, the voter emits a VOTER_ERROR, sets `attempts=0`, and STILL defers vote-less (voter.py:538-548) — a new error path introduced by this diff with observable behavior (a distinct VOTER_ERROR marker and a deferral that would otherwise never escalate). No test injects a record_attempt failure to assert this fail-open-on-the-counter, never-on-the-vote contract.
